description: Dan Dan Noodles are a classic Sichuan street food, known for their irresistible combination of spicy, savory, nutty, and slightly sweet flavors. This iconic dish features tender noodles tossed in a rich, aromatic sauce, topped with crispy minced pork and vibrant greens. Prepare to embark on a culinary journey that will awaken your taste buds with every slurp.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pork Topping
instructions.text: Heat cooking oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground pork and stir-fry, breaking it apart, until it is cooked through and slightly crispy. Drain any excess fat. Add Shaoxing wine and soy sauce, stir well. Finally, add the finely minced Sichuan preserved mustard green (ya cai) and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In each serving bowl, combine Sichuan chili oil, sesame paste, light soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, sugar, Sichuan peppercorn powder, and minced garlic. Whisk these ingredients together until well combined and smooth. Add 2-3 tablespoons of hot chicken stock or hot water to thin the sauce to your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Cook the Noodles
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add the Chinese egg noodles and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Fresh noodles usually take 2-3 minutes, dried noodles may take longer.

instructions.title: Blanch Greens (Optional)
instructions.text: If using, quickly blanch bok choy or spinach in the same boiling water for about 30 seconds until tender-crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

instructions.title: Assemble the Bowls
instructions.text: Once the noodles are cooked, drain them well. Immediately divide the hot noodles among the prepared serving bowls, placing them directly over the sauce base.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Top each bowl of noodles generously with the prepared crispy pork and ya cai topping. Garnish with chopped roasted peanuts, fresh scallions, and blanched greens if desired. Before eating, instruct diners to thoroughly mix all the ingredients in the bowl to coat the noodles evenly with the flavorful sauce. Serve immediately.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use freshly ground Sichuan peppercorns. Toast them lightly in a dry pan before grinding to release their full aroma and numbing sensation.

Chinese sesame paste is crucial; it is different from tahini. If unavailable, use a blend of roasted sesame seeds and a neutral oil, ground until smooth, but be aware the flavor profile will slightly change.
Always mix Dan Dan Noodles thoroughly before eating. The sauce sits at the bottom of the bowl, and a good mix ensures every strand of noodle is coated in the rich, complex flavors.
